J U D G M E NT /AWAR D 1.

Vide this judgment/award, I shall dispose off DAR filed by IO SI Netar Singh, PS Begumpur, in regard to death of Smt. Malti Devi, (in short, the deceased), who died in a road vehicular accident on 13.09.2022.
2. Brief facts as per DAR Ex. PW1/2 are that on 13.09.2022 at 01:59 hours the deceased was travelling in RTV bus bearing registration no. DL 1VC 1580 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle).
The deceased had boarded the bus for Begumpur.

When the deceased was in the process of deboarding the offending vehicle, near PS Begumpur, driver of the offending vehicle did not stop the offending vehicle due to which deceased fell down from the bus.
After that driver stopped the offending vehicle.
The conductor on the said bus made the deceased sit on the road side.
In the meanwhile, PCR also came there and deceased was taken to BSA Hospital.
The information of accident was lodged at PS vide DD no. 121A.

From BSA Hospital, deceased was referred to Safdarjung Hospital where she expired during treatment on 15.09.2022.
3.

As per DAR and investigation conducted by IO, R1 was driving the MACT Case No. 215/2023 (FIR no. 707/2022) Rama Shanker Vs. Kaushal Kumar & Anr Page no. 2 of 13 VIKRAM Date:
offending vehicle in negligent manner which caused the accident resulting in death of deceased.

sentences.text: Cause of death, confirmed by PM report no. 2462/22, was cranio-cerebral damage as a result of blunt force trauma to the head.

As such R1 was charge-sheeted for offences under section 279/304A IPC.
4.
As per DAR deceased survived by her husband and two minor sons (hereinafter referred to as Petitioner No. 1 to 3).
5. No WS/reply was filed on behalf of R1 & R2.
Therefore, they were proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 24.05.2023.

He relied on photocopy of his aadhar card and copy of DAR as Ex.Pw1/1 & Ex.Pw1/2(colly).
He is not the eye witness of the incident.
He admitted that deceased was not working anywhere at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that his affidavit Ex.Pw1/A is false and fabricated.
9. Petitioner has also brought Sh. Ashish Gaurav in his evidence and examined him as Pw2.
Pw2 had made call to the police informing about the accident.
During cross examination, he admitted that the deceased had already fallen on the road.
He voluntarily stated that conductor of the bus told him that a lady fell down from the RTV bus.
10. Petitioner has also examined Ct. Girraj as Pw3 who deposed that on 13.09.2022 at about 02;00 pm, he was coming towards PS from 100 foota road on government motorcycle.
On seeing the crowd, he stopped the motorcycle and saw that lady was lying on the divider and was bleeding from head.
He also deposed that conductor of the bus was also there who had money in his hand and RTV bearing registration no. DL 1VC 1580 was also standing there.

sentences.text: civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

In view of the facts disclose in the DAR which proves place of incident as well as caused of death and on the basis of aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle, which is clearly visible and as such, was responsible not only for this accident, but also for everything that followed thereafter.
Accordingly issue no.1 is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

18.
As this Tribunal has already held that R1 was responsible for the death of the deceased due to his neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Therefore, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensated for death of deceased in the above accident, but computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.

sentences.text: As already stated above, the claimant/petitioners are husband and children of deceased.
As per aadhar card of deceased, deceased was about 28 years old on the date of accident.
However, no document is placed on record to show the income of deceased and no documents pertaining to education status of the deceased was also filed.
It is stated by petitioner that the deceased was home maker.
Therefore, the income of the deceased, as on the date of the accident, has been treated as that of "un-skilled".
Therefore, on the date of accident i.e 13.09.2022, the minimum wages of an un-skilled in Delhi is Rs. 16,506/- per month.
Counsel for the petitioners further argued that future prospects should also be awarded to the petitioners as per law.
Ld. Counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the deceased was the sole member looking after the petitioner and her minor children.

LIABILITY 29.
Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
The offending vehicle was insured with R3.
But it is claimed by R3 that the driving licence of driver/R1 of the offending vehicle was not valid to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

In Bajaj Allianze General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Rambha Devi & Ors.
2024 INSC 840 it was observed by Hon'ble Supreme Court that even if the vehicle was purchased for commercial purpose and was for commercial use, the driver who was having LMV is also authorized to ply the vehicle, unless it is shown that the weight of the vehicle exceeds 7500 kg.

entities.text:
Bajaj Allianze General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Rambha Devi & Ors.
2024 INSC 840
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per vehicle particulars, annexed with the DAR, the unladen weight of the offending vehicle is 2840 kg and thus Insurance Company cannot dispute liability on this account.
Moreover, the driving licence of R1 is valid till 29.06.2022 for transport vehicle and the accident is of 13.09.2022.
That does not mean that the R1 was not qualified to ply the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the submission of R3 not to compensate the petitioner is not accepted.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
My issue wise findings in the case are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1 1. Whether deceased Malti Devi W/o Sh. Rama Shankar expired due to injuries suffered in road traffic accident on 13.09.2022 at about 01:59 P.M., at 100 Foota Road, Deep Vihar, near Red Light, Sector 23, Rohini due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing no.
DL-1VC-1580 which was being driven by driver Sh. Kaushal Kumar S/o Sh. Ram Mohan Kumar, on the said date, time and place?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death : (a) age of the deceased; (b) income of the deceased; and the (c) the number of dependents.
